topic: Testing Terraform locally with an AWS emulator to speed up CI and save money
postText:
Testing Terraform locally? You can spin an AWS emulator in minutes.

- I tried the new AWS emulator to run Terraform plans without a real account. It boots a tiny EC2-compatible API that understands VPC, S3, and IAM, letting me catch syntax errors early.

- The biggest win is speed: a full plan that used to take 30 seconds on the cloud now finishes in under 5 seconds on my laptop. That translates to faster CI pipelines and cheaper test runs.

- There are limits: the emulator doesn’t simulate every service (e.g., DynamoDB streams) and some resource attributes differ slightly. I keep a small integration test suite that hits the real AWS once a day to catch drift.

- Cost savings are real. My team cut dev-environment AWS spend by roughly $150 per month by swapping nightly sandbox builds for the emulator. It also reduces the blast radius of accidental resource creation.

- The community is already contributing plugins to extend the emulator with RDS, Lambda, and even CloudWatch metrics. I tried a third-party RDS mock and it let me validate DB schema migrations without spinning a real instance.

What tricks have you discovered for safe, cheap Terraform testing?
